Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
233 AM EDT Sat Aug 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 233 AM EDT Saturday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 233 AM EDT Saturday...

1. Intervals of showers and thunderstorms will continue 
throughout the day. Warm and humid conditions will persist through 
much of the weekend. 

2. Chances for showers and thunderstorms continue to look 
likely for late Monday into Tuesday as a cold front pushes through 
the region.  

3. Periodic showers and thunderstorms are expected next week as 
temperatures cool back to and eventually slightly below seasonal 
averages. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 233 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Warm and humid conditions are expected to persist 
throughout the day today with plenty of moisture streaming into the 
region as we remain in between a Bermuda High and an upper low 
centered over Hudson Bay. Shower activity this morning continues 
across the region, slowly moving northeastward. Heavy rainfall has 
been the main concern with these storms, as several locations have 
received over 2 inches of rainfall within rather short periods of 
time, for example Essex County, NY where Flash Flood Warnings were 
issued overnight. Precipitation is expected to wane towards the 
morning, before additional rounds of convection develop later in the 
day. Model soundings show CAPE values of 1500 J/kg or so, with 
relatively low wind shear, with the environment favorable for pulse 
thunderstorms. Any thunderstorms that develop will likely be garden-
variety, but a stronger storm can't be entirely ruled out. The main 
concern this afternoon will once again be heavy rainfall and any 
possible hydrological/flooding concerns, especially in locations 
have already received decent rainfall over the last few days. WPC 
continues to have a Marginal ERO across the region for tomorrow. 
Another round of showers is expected to move through the region 
tonight into Sunday, although with little instability these showers 
should be rather unimpactful. A brief break in the unsettled pattern 
is expected to develop through the day Sunday as a narrow axis of 
high pressure moves over the region.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A brief period of high pressure will bring relatively 
tranquil weather to start the week, but unsettled weather is 
expected to return Monday evening ahead of an approaching cold 
front. The threat of showers and thunderstorms will ramp up 
throughout the evening, with a bulk of the precipitation expected 
overnight into early Tuesday.Stronger storms currently look unlikely 
with only modest instability and shear, but we'll have to monitor 
any trends in the data if they deviate from the current thinking. 
Temperatures on Monday will be a few degrees cooler, with high 
temperatures in the mid 70s to mid 80s across the region.

KEY MESSAGE 3: The long wave pattern is projected to remain zonal 
across the Northeast through next week with unblocked flow 
downstream and largely the result of a massive Omega High centered 
over the Western US and Canada. The result will be for quick moving 
systems tracking through the long wave pattern bringing periodic 
showers and thunderstorms. The nature of this pattern will promote 
weaker systems and lean towards a slow cooling trend with 
temperatures favored to dip below seasonal averages by the end of 
the work week as the Bermuda High retreats southeastward. As such, 
highs in the 80s Tuesday will decrease into the mid/upper 70s by 
Friday.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 06Z Sunday...Intermittent showers will continue through 08Z
for most terminals keeping MVFR CIGs/VIS potentially impacting
aviators. After 08Z, any clearing will result in rapid stratus/fog
formation for susceptible locations like SLK/MPV with lower
potential for more widespread IFR conditions. VFR conditions return
after 12Z with showers returning 18-00Z. More fog and MVFR/IFR
conditions are possible after 00Z tonight, but will be dependent on
how quickly clouds can clear.

Outlook...

Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Chance TSRA.

Tuesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA.
Wednesday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
